# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Kushi

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
UI/UX design, travelling in Germany with the Deutschlandticket and drawing.

## Fun fact
I visited eight German cities with the Deutschlandticket and got lost at every Hauptbahnhof.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is great for quick prototypes. I can go from an idea to a working UI in one afternoon. But the designs often look the same and a bit boring. AI does the first 80 percent, but the last 20 percent still needs a human.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Making software will be very fast, so good ideas and good user experience will matter most. Small teams with AI will do what big teams do today. I hope design and accessibility finally get more attention.

## My hot take on AI
AI will make every app look the same, so good design will be the most valuable skill in tech.

# Om

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Cybersecurity, football and mechanical keyboards.

## Fun fact
I have more mechanical keyboards than shoes.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI writes code very fast, but it also writes unsafe code very fast. I have seen it suggest passwords directly in the code. It is useful, but only if you know enough to see the mistakes.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
AI agents will check the code of other AI agents for security problems. Developers will need to know about new attacks like prompt injection. Less people will write code, more people will check it.

## My hot take on AI
The first big AI agent hack has not happened yet. But it will come, and it will start with a README file.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Kushi

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
UI/UX design, travelling in Germany with the Deutschlandticket and drawing.

## Fun fact
I visited eight German cities with the Deutschlandticket and got lost at every Hauptbahnhof.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is great for quick prototypes. I can go from an idea to a working UI in one afternoon. But the designs often look the same and a bit boring. AI does the first 80 percent, but the last 20 percent still needs a human.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Making software will be very fast, so good ideas and good user experience will matter most. Small teams with AI will do what big teams do today. I hope design and accessibility finally get more attention.

## My hot take on AI
AI will make every app look the same, so good design will be the most valuable skill in tech.

# Om

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Cybersecurity, football and mechanical keyboards.

## Fun fact
I have more mechanical keyboards than shoes.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI writes code very fast, but it also writes unsafe code very fast. I have seen it suggest passwords directly in the code. It is useful, but only if you know enough to see the mistakes.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
AI agents will check the code of other AI agents for security problems. Developers will need to know about new attacks like prompt injection. Less people will write code, more people will check it.

## My hot take on AI
The first big AI agent hack has not happened yet. But it will come, and it will start with a README file.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Kushi

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
UI/UX design, travelling in Germany with the Deutschlandticket and drawing.

## Fun fact
I visited eight German cities with the Deutschlandticket and got lost at every Hauptbahnhof.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is great for quick prototypes. I can go from an idea to a working UI in one afternoon. But the designs often look the same and a bit boring. AI does the first 80 percent, but the last 20 percent still needs a human.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Making software will be very fast, so good ideas and good user experience will matter most. Small teams with AI will do what big teams do today. I hope design and accessibility finally get more attention.

## My hot take on AI
AI will make every app look the same, so good design will be the most valuable skill in tech.

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

Cybersecurity, football and mechanical keyboards.

I have more mechanical keyboards than shoes.

AI writes code very fast, but it also writes unsafe code very fast. I have seen it suggest passwords directly in the code. It is useful, but only if you know enough to see the mistakes.

The first big AI agent hack has not happened yet. But it will come, and it will start with a README file.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

## Study background

Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Krish

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Web development (MERN stack), chess and playing piano.

## Fun fact
I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
I think AI agents will write most of the code. Developers will spend more time checking, testing and deciding what to build. The important skill will be knowing if the code is actually correct.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Gouthami

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

## Fun fact
I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

## My hot take on AI
If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

## Interests

I play bullet chess with around 2000 rating, so I can make bad moves really fast.

AI is really good for simple and repeated code. It can make a basic MERN app in a few minutes. But sometimes it uses functions that don't even exist, so I always have to check its code. For me it is a helper, not a replacement.

## My hot take on AI
AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

--- Result 1: SG-18 ---
[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy
Status: ACTIVE
Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

--- Result 2: SG-19 ---
[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1)
Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.

--- Result 3: SG-21 ---
[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

--- Result 4: SG-20 ---
[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Data visualisation, dancing and baking (my cakes don't always rise).

I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

I use AI a lot to understand new libraries and error messages, and it helps a lot. But it sounds very sure even when it is wrong, so I always check the documentation. I think the danger is that students stop learning the basics.

If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

# Chirag

## Study background
M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester, Paderborn University.

## Interests
Machine learning, cricket and finding the best Döner in Paderborn.

## Fun fact
I have a list of every Döner I ate in Germany with ratings, and it is longer than my list of thesis ideas.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today
AI tools save me a lot of time for small things like tests and short scripts. But in big projects it forgets the context and starts guessing. I use it like a fast intern. Helpful, but I check everything.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years
Coding will be more like managing AI agents than typing code yourself. Planning and design will be more important than syntax. Maybe "AI code debugger" will be a real job.

## My hot take on AI
Prompt engineering is just writing clear requirements, and we were always bad at that.

I learned more German from supermarket labels than from my German class.

People will build simple apps just by describing them in normal language. Testing and checking data will become a bigger part of the job. Understanding the problem will be more important than knowing one framework.

If you can't explain the code the AI wrote, then you didn't build it. You just copied a guess.

AI will not take your job, but a junior with 3 AI agents and no code review can break production.

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics
Status: ACTIVE
The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

--- Result 2: SG-22 ---
[SG-22] Theme toggle control
Status: ACTIVE
- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.

- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.
